selected_bottleneck: changeset-apply-control-boundary-revalidation（变更集应用时控制路径边界重验证）
selected_problem: Fresh main blocked new control-path changesets at stage time, but ChangesetStore.apply still trusted persisted STAGED documents. A changeset staged before the boundary hardening (or otherwise persisted with an old valid format) could still apply a .git/config change after upgrading, so the invariant was not migration-safe across the durable stage→apply boundary.
decision_basis: Changesets are durable runtime artifacts and apply is a later effectful boundary, so safety rules that only exist at stage time do not cover already-persisted STAGED artifacts.
Revalidating the existing blocked-path rule at apply time is a narrow invariant repair; rollback intentionally remains available so already-applied legacy artifacts can still be reverted.
Hosted Developer Execution Runtime remained temporarily unavailable with HTTP 502, so this cycle uses DWAC_SOURCE_CONTRACT_REPLAY（DWAC 源码契约重放） and does not claim a hosted DWAC success receipt.

pre_fix_reality.source_observation: Fresh main ChangesetStore.apply checked ancestor/preimage identity and mode but had no blocked control-path revalidation before writing persisted changes.
pre_fix_reality.impact: a legacy STAGED .git control-path changeset could survive an upgrade and still cross the newly established staging boundary

change: The blocked control-path predicate is shared inside ChangesetStore and is enforced both when staging and immediately before apply preflight. Rollback is deliberately not blocked, preserving reversibility for already-applied legacy changesets.

validation.node_check: PASS on the exact proposed core/changesets.mjs content
validation.focused_legacy_changeset_replay: PASS: a persisted STAGED .git/config write is rejected before mutation; an already-APPLIED legacy .git/config changeset remains rollback-capable and restores the original content

truth_boundary: This makes the existing control-path invariant migration-safe at stage→apply while preserving rollback. It does not prove general runtime-artifact tamper resistance, staged postimage integrity, credential-write policy, filesystem-wide case/Unicode identity, or arbitrary complex repository synthesis.
